subject: Marketplace fee split & commit-tier discounting — allocation options
messages:
From: Susan Hawkins <susan.hawkins@amazon.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace margin / commit-tier question for Acme deal

Hi Dylan,

Following up from our connect last week about the Acme Corp listing. They are evaluating a committed usage path but procurement asked about how marketplace fees affect the customer-visible discount tiers. AWS Marketplace normally charges a percent fee on the gross price at the marketplace level (standard pass-through), and Acme wants clarity on the net they receive and how commits are calculated.

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood outline how you would apply per-token discounts when the contract is transacted through AWS Marketplace vs direct invoicing?
- Is Redwood able to either absorb the marketplace fee, or provide a defined gross-to-net reconciliation so Acme's committed thresholds don't move?

Looping in Aditya to help with arithmetic and Lauras from rev ops if needed. Also copy of the current Acme RFP attached for context.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Hawkins
Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
[Attachment: acme_rfp_sorted.pdf (pdf, 145KB)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Susan Hawkins <susan.hawkins@amazon.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace margin / commit-tier question for Acme deal

Susan — thanks for the clear note. High level answers up front:

1) Marketplace vs direct: list (gross) price is what shows in the AWS listing. Marketplace applies its fee (typically 7% in our conversations) and remits net to Redwood. For customers, the invoice they see from AWS will reflect the list pricing minus any discounts we configure in the marketplace offer.

2) Commit tiers: commits are usually structured on the customer-visible spend (gross list price) unless we explicitly build a gross-to-net protection into the commercial terms. If Acme wants their committed thresholds to be based on net receipts (post-marketplace fee), we can do one of the approaches below.

Attached is a draft fee model (redwood_marketplace_fee_model_v2.xlsx) with worked examples. Short proposals:
- Option A — Retail parity, Redwood absorbs fee: Redwood quotes the same per-token list price on marketplace as direct, Redwood accepts the marketplace fee (7%) out of our margin. Commit thresholds measured on gross list price, customer sees identical numbers to direct buying.
- Option B — Gross-to-net safeguard: We keep a customer-facing per-token discount that maps to the direct price. At settlement, Redwood calculates the marketplace fee and issues a credit to Acme (or adjusts future invoices) so that their effective commit credit is equal to the direct path. This requires reconciliation cadence (monthly/quarterly) and a contract clause.
- Option C — Adjusted list pricing: Increase the marketplace list price to cover the marketplace fee so net to Redwood equals direct-case net. This keeps accounting straightforward but means the customer-visible price is slightly higher unless we reflect an equivalent off-list discount.

Example numbers in the sheet show how a 30M token commit with a 10% per-token discount behaves under each option.

Quick ask back: what marketplace fee % are you seeing for this listing and do you have standard timing for settlement/reconciliation? If AWS definitely retains 7% and settlement is monthly, Option B is likely the least disruptive for Acme's commit certainty.

Happy to sync for 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_marketplace_fee_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 82KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Susan Hawkins <susan.hawkins@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace margin / commit-tier question for Acme deal

Adding a couple implementation notes from pricing ops:
- If we go with Option B (gross-to-net credits), we need a reconciliation flow and a template credit memo. Ops prefers quarterly reconciliations for deals this size to keep ledger churn manageable.
- Margin target: for this segment we aim for a net margin floor of ~25% after marketplace fees and variable infra costs. The spreadsheet shows a corner case where Option A would push us below that target for the 30M token band unless we push smaller discounts.
- For Option C, legal will need to approve the marketplace list price being higher than direct MSRPs; that can create procurement friction but is simplest for our finance team.

If Acme is sensitive to list price visibility, recommend Option B with quarterly reconciliation and a small protection band (e.g., Redwood covers first 1% of marketplace fee variance).

-Aditya
Head of Pricing & Revenue Ops

From: Susan Hawkins <susan.hawkins@amazon.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Acme Corp Procurement <contracts@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace margin / commit-tier question for Acme deal

Thanks for the quick turnaround — helpful. A few clarifying points from the marketplace side:
- The standard AWS Marketplace transaction fee for this catalog type is 7%, settled monthly. We can request a variance but expect ~7% in our planning.
- AWS can support a Marketplace Offset arrangement (where sellers issue credits) but that's a negotiated commercial commitment and may add listing approval steps.
- We typically recommend that sellers outline the credit/reconciliation cadence in their purchase terms so procurement can map to their forecasting.

Acme procurement: do you have a preference? If you want commit thresholds to be measured on the net cash to Redwood, we can accept a credit approach so the contract reads that committed spend is measured net of marketplace fees, with monthly reconciliation. If Acme prefers simple invoices from AWS and no post-transaction credits, then commits will be measured on gross list spend and the customer-visible discount tier needs to reflect that.

Susan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Susan Hawkins <susan.hawkins@amazon.com>, Acme Corp Procurement <contracts@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace margin / commit-tier question for Acme deal

Acme / Susan — thanks. To keep the deal moving, here's a concrete path I suggest:

1) Use Option B (gross-to-net credits) with monthly settlement: Redwood will list the same customer-facing per-token discounts in AWS so Acme's procurement sees parity with direct pricing.
2) Contract language: committed spend is defined as "customer spend net of marketplace transaction fees" and Redwood will issue a monthly credit to reconcile the marketplace fee so that the effective credit toward the commit equals the direct-path credit.
3) Reconciliation cadence: monthly statements, quarterly settlement of any +/- deltas. Ops note: we'll cap Redwood's exposure to the first 1% of marketplace fee variance; anything beyond will be treated as a billing adjustment to the customer.

If Acme approves that approach I will: (a) update the MSA redline with the clause, (b) attach the fee model for your procurement team to review, and (c) set a 30 minute call with Susan + Aditya + Laura to align on settlement mechanics.

Proposed meeting windows: Wed 8/11 10:00-10:30am PT or Thu 8/12 2:00-2:30pm PT.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
